milestones.name: Touchdown
milestones.fact: The Soviet Luna 9 probe made the first soft landing on the Moon on February 3, 1966.

milestones.name: Odometer
milestones.fact: Apollo 17's Lunar Roving Vehicle covered about 36 km across three drives in December 1972.

milestones.name: Mapper
milestones.fact: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter has mapped the Moon since 2009; its laser altimeter measured the terrain you are driving on.

milestones.name: Crater descent
milestones.fact: Without wind or rain to wear them down, lunar craters keep their shape for hundreds of millions of years.

milestones.name: Boulder field
milestones.fact: Almost all boulders on the lunar surface are smaller than 4 m; most were thrown out by impacts.

milestones.name: Into the dark
milestones.fact: Craters near the lunar poles that never see sunlight measure about 33 to 38 K, around -238 °C.

milestones.name: Flare survivor
milestones.fact: With no thick atmosphere or global magnetic field, the lunar surface is exposed directly to radiation from solar flares.

milestones.name: Clean run
milestones.fact: ISRO's Pragyan rover was designed to work for one lunar daylight period, about 14 Earth days.

milestones.name: Crater layers
milestones.fact: Crater walls expose layers of older rock and debris, giving geologists a look back in time.

milestones.name: Regolith sample
milestones.fact: The six Apollo landings brought back 382 kg of lunar rock, core samples, pebbles, sand and dust.

milestones.name: Water ice
milestones.fact: In 2009 NASA's LCROSS impact found about 4 to 6% water by weight in Cabeus crater near the south pole.

milestones.name: Earth on the horizon
milestones.fact: From the lunar south pole Earth sits low on the horizon and can dip below it.

milestones.name: Rim panorama
milestones.fact: The de Gerlache crater rim is one of the regions NASA has considered for Artemis landings near the south pole.
